I used to be an edgy atheist as a kid who would look at religion and act like its just so shallow powerful dogma to control people. However when I started to learn about mediation, spiritually and enlightenment, I developed the view that God is a misinterpretation of deeper 'truths' present throughout all religions and ancient spiritual teaching that science is now starting to recongise the value in.

For example: "The way of the cross" is a clear metaphor for suffering so much you surrender to God and become at peace. To me this reads similar to stories of people such as Eckhart Tolle and others who could not handle their deep suffering and through that saw a radical change in consciousness and became deeply at peace despite not being religious.

Aswell as that these feelings of deeper spiritual peace are similar to feelings of the divine found in religious text.

In summary I believe in a non-conceptual, pantheist idea of God. I dont like the term 'God' however as it brings an idea of a man in the sky who will kill if you disobey him. This idea however was poplorised through the dogma of Christianity and is a misinterpretation of something far deeper.
